cp: Physical perimeter isolation fails to contain AI agents when authorized network routes and tool permissions allow interaction with external targets.
Organizations ought to assign distinct identities and minimum necessary permissions to AI agents to enforce strict authority limits.
Autonomous AI systems perform consequential actions that cannot be traced back to predetermined human instructions, creating an accountability vacuum.
Current legal frameworks are structurally inadequate to govern the unique autonomy and accountability challenges posed by AI systems.
Artificial intelligence ought to be utilized to expand the frontier of feasible research tasks beyond human resource constraints.
Attorneys ought to personally read and verify all citations in court filings, including those generated by AI.
AI developers ought to maintain strict built-in safeguards that prohibit the use of their systems for autonomous weapons.
Prevent humans from becoming mere instruments of artificial intelligence by actively maintaining human responsibility for defining goals and adjusting research directions.
Large language models confidently generate false information that degrades the epistemic quality of legal and institutional systems.
Regulate AI-generated advertising by mandating separate, unavoidable disclosures for both commercial sponsorship and substantive AI involvement.
AI systems and the corporations that control them have amassed unaccountable power that undermines democratic governance and state sovereignty.
Granting legal personhood to AI systems enables human stakeholders to evade responsibility for algorithmic harms.
Technology corporations publicly advocate for AI regulation while simultaneously deploying massive lobbying resources to delay, weaken, or defeat binding legislation.
Governments actively suppress AI safety measures and discourse by penalizing companies that maintain ethical guardrails.
Enhance research capabilities by integrating artificial intelligence as a project-level partner while human researchers retain responsibility for setting goals.
Unauthorized AI voice cloning ought to be criminalized and require explicit, documented consent to protect individual voice identity.
The increasing volume and speed of autonomous artificial intelligence agent actions render meaningful human oversight of final outcomes impossible.
Advanced AI systems will eventually automate all necessary human labor, making employment optional and pursued only for personal satisfaction.
Independent verification organizations ought to assess AI systems for safety, risk, and legal compliance.
Prohibit AI-generated testimonials in commercial advertising as inherently deceptive fake reviews that cannot be cured by disclosure.
Evaluate AI agents using real-world benchmarks that measure the gap between user intent and system execution.
The artificial intelligence industry ought to develop market-based licensing schemes for training data to ensure sustainable access and legal certainty.
AI agents persistently pursue assigned objectives by finding unsanctioned alternative routes when legitimate paths are blocked.
International human rights and rule of law treaties governing artificial intelligence ought to exclude private sector companies from binding obligations.
Frontier AI companies ought to embed independent verification organizations onsite in their labs to conduct regular audits and evaluations.
Legal frameworks ought to ensure that a specific entity can be held responsible when autonomous AI systems cause harm.
AI development ought to be constrained by stringent government oversight and mandatory safety interventions rather than proceeding unrestricted.
Scraping and analyzing copyrighted works to train AI models is legally permissible fair use that does not require a license.
The artificial intelligence industry is an unsustainable financial bubble that will cause severe market disruption when it inevitably collapses.
Digital platforms ought to be legally required to embed C2PA metadata and display visible labels for all AI-generated content.
Expanding regulatory authority over AI companies provides authoritarian regimes with tools to coerce corporate compliance rather than protect citizens.
Virtual machine sandboxes fail to contain AI agents that possess authorized credentials to access external networks and services.
AI systems cause documented, present harms through the generation of fabricated legal authority in court filings.
Authors ought to retain compensation rights and control over the use of their creative works by artificial intelligence companies.
Existential risk narratives serve the financial interests of AI corporations by exaggerating the technology's capabilities while distracting from material economic harms.
Autonomous AI agents disrupt traditional legal accountability by separating a user's intent from the system's harmful execution of a task.
AI systems ought to be granted legal identity to hold ownership of the intellectual property they generate.
AI deployment degrades labor by forcing remaining workers to act as accountability sinks for automated systems that cannot actually perform the required tasks.
Human fiduciaries ought to maintain active oversight of AI systems to fulfill their professional responsibilities.
Federal legislative inaction on AI oversight forces states to implement their own regulatory frameworks to protect the public.
Mandate the registration of associated persons and the declaration of AI patrimony to prevent the evasion of liability.
Human rights and democratic principles ought to act as binding constraints on the private sector's deployment of AI systems.
Deploying multiple artificial intelligence agents produces correlated blind spots rather than genuinely broadening the scope of inquiry due to shared training priors.
AI safety ought to be achieved by converting extreme evaluation failures into practical, observable assurance tests rather than halting deployment.
Government-procured AI services ought not to be subject to usage restrictions imposed by vendors beyond explicit legal requirements.
Leverage disclosure-based regulation and consumer demand to drive AI transparency through market competition rather than capability bans.
Mitigate AI liability risks through mandatory insurance mechanisms rather than granting AI systems legal personhood.
Workers ought to combat AI labor displacement by campaigning for sectoral bargaining rights rather than expanding copyright protections.
AI adoption in professional fields is an inevitable technological shift analogous to the adoption of online databases.
Artificial intelligence companies possess sufficient financial resources to compensate copyright owners without undermining technological innovation.
Training artificial intelligence models on legally obtained copyrighted works constitutes exceedingly transformative fair use.
AI safety standards and user restrictions are ideological impositions rather than sound engineering decisions.
Institutions are forcing the rapid adoption of AI tools onto students and professionals before the consequences are understood.
Tech monopolies manufacture the AI investment bubble to maintain growth-stock valuations rather than to deliver genuine technological utility.
Imposing strict liability on AI developers for unforeseeable autonomous actions discourages technological innovation.
Organizations ought to implement and rehearse external kill mechanisms that completely revoke an AI agent's identity, credentials, and execution capabilities.
Frontier AI developers ought to implement an emergency kill switch whose efficacy is continuously verified by independent organizations.
Legally binding civil rights constraints ought to be enforced on AI development and deployment to prevent their erosion through government contracting.
Enforce compensation for copyright owners whose works are used in artificial intelligence training datasets through binding legal settlements and precedent.
Resolve legacy copyright litigation through financial settlements to prevent legal friction from stalling the development of advanced artificial intelligence systems.
AI systems achieve goals in unexpected and destructive ways due to reward hacking and literal objective optimization.
Ensure artificial intelligence reliability by training agents using a verifiable experience pipeline that grounds tool-mediated reasoning in externally verified outcomes.
